searchText: not sure if you saw the discussion between <@273808422753796097> and <@1126229231572094976> a few days ago on the 8141 signal chat, but they raised a point that for an account to use leanPCS for authentication, the account contract would need to run PIOP over the PCS claims, but since the PCS claims depend on the sighash, if we run the PIOP in a VERIFY frame (whose calldata is committed to sighash), we have a circular dependency PIOP -> PCS claims -> sighash -> PIOP. if we run PIOP in a proof frame along with the PCS openings, we lose the benefit of aggregation so it seems that we'd need either 1) a type of PROOF frame whose calldata is readable from VERIFY frames, or 2) we go back to the siglist design with the ARBITRARY bytes which are readable in VERIFY frames i personally prefer the siglist approach just because again the proof data is more like dependencies whose ordering doesn't matter. and to enable L2s to permissionlessly deploy new schemes, maybe we could just replace the siglist scheme ID with verifier address instead? <@427491045308235776> I was thinking that if the objective is really 1) given the current size of sphincs.art I'd rather go with SPHINCS+ (it's almost same size) To me its not clear that we can definitively say that we will do PROOF with no aggregation, or PROOF with just builder aggregation or PROOF with mempool aggregation at this point in time. Though it does seem clear that we need to gather data on the different scenarios where PROOF with no aggregation is the simplest lift from `bogota-devnet-2`. Even if we were to go with SPHINCS+, it seems that we will still need to know what are the bandwidth and resource requirements for it, which should hopefully inform us on what is the appropriate size for the signature scheme if the current size is not enough Though changing the signature scheme in the devnets is not very difficult (its mainly upgrading leanVM repo and pushing another release) > Even if we were to go with SPHINCS+, it seems that we will still need to know what are the bandwidth and resource requirements for it, which should hopefully inform us on what is the appropriate size for the signature scheme if the current size is not enough It feels like we keep going back and forth between: we need to understand bandwidth and resource requirements to know which sig scheme to go for, and the exact opposite (we need to settle the sig scheme and that will allow to understand what we need on the networking side) if we can choose which one we settle first, what the order should be between the two it seems like a good first step (imo easier to settle the signature scheme first) the problem is that different signatures are optimized according to the scenario we want to cover : e.g. aggregation vs not aggregation . But yeah I agree with <@427491045308235776> when he says it is easy to switch signature scheme in the testnet. Speaking of which , <@808969530608451584> are we still running the old parameters correct (not the sphincs.art one) well iiuc there also many other parameters that determine which sig scheme we choose, aggregation vs not aggregation is just one of them Thinking out loud There is some signature size that we cannot handle on the network without sacrificing hardware/bandwidth requirements. For example, 10MB signature sizes are not possible. To me, its not clear whether the limit is 8KB or 5KB and what the exact relationship to bandwidth is here. Is this clear to folks? This was one of the reasons, I was proposing to do a layered approach, ie which signature scheme makes sense without aggregation and whats the relationship there. Then which signature scheme makes sense with aggregation, or what are the tradeoffs there. Then it _seems_ like we could make an informed decision on doing no aggregation in H* that's what I meant by freezing the sig scheme based on other dimensions (not node resources), e.g., security of the scheme, complexity/auditability, wallet friendliness, etc.. rather than trying to change the scheme based on networking because things still feel blurry there If we want to measure the different variants we need to make it easy on the client side to enable and disable the three options and then measure them, that might be easier than having three devnets? by variants, do you mean different parameters for the signature scheme or do you mean a network with and without aggregation? This seems to me an important analysis we should make. This is not clear to me also. Not sure if <@857052906495017000> has data on this? If not, happy to help on such analysis Would you want to do simulations? I think right now we would need the PROOF without aggregation specs to be implemented before being able to take analyse data from devnet runs Basically both, can't we support multiple signature schemes via different transaction types or just via frames and can we have flags to enable / disable mempool aggregation or builder aggregation I don't know yet how much we can do with simulations vs devnets. I can chat with <@857052906495017000> and let you know I was mostly imagining the PIOP would happen as part of the PROOF frame even if you did the PIOP in the account contract, if you use the canonical signing hash you wouldn't commit to any sig hash in the calldata? and if you wanted to do something other than the canonical signing hash, you would have to construct it yourself in the account anyways? why can't you run PIOP along with PCS opening? you can run them together but then the openings sit in the verifier's calldata and don't get aggregated, and the openings are basically the heavy part leanPCS wants aggregated to aggregate them they need to be their own claims but when the proof is the signature, those claims depend on the sig hash, and in a proof frame the claim is covered by it (which is the loop we're trying to avoid) is there a write up of this? It seems that folks are in-favour of shipping H* without aggregation, which was why I thought it would be good to have that separately. We could merge builder aggregation and mempool aggregation and then have a flag somewhere for that though? mostly here: https://github.com/leanEthereum/leanPCS/blob/main/eip-draft_leanPCS.md#how-a-proof-signs-its-transaction and here's Kev's new PR: https://github.com/kevaundray/EIPs/pull/7 Yeah maybe when we are in the builder aggregation devnet, then we can implement mempool aggregation on top of that and enable it via CLI flag. But I don’t really see a reason to optimize the amount of devnets PQTS call starts in 10 minutes 📣 toni has a writeup with the PIOP flow: https://hackmd.io/@Nerolation/BJEQraRAGe I added a `PROOF_READ_FLAG` so now you can have a proof frame with PIOP data and read it from a VERIFY frame without it being hashed into the signing hash <@427491045308235776> didn't get to read your answer in <@968526635735326741>'s thread <@725415098331430932> impact of the parameters on the signature https://ethresear.ch/t/sphincs-minus-efficient-stateless-post-quantum-signature-verification-on-the-evm/25165 As you can see there is a lot we can do to offload to the signer without losing the lifetime or security level. The one missing piece in that article is pruning which was presented later by conduition https://conduition.io/cryptography/hypertree-pruning/ and basically replaced the "JARDIN" follow up which was a weird smart contract system to have fast signing. Solving the privacy problem in pruning courtesy of our Emile : Pruning Use a single, large, XMSS layer. Weak devices only construct a subtree of 2ᵇ leaves, and use pseudorandom nodes for the rest, and signing grinds until its index lands in it (An idea from conduition). Verifier algo is unaffected. The risk of reusing a seed under different pruning parameters is fixed by deriving a second seed as H(seed ‖ parameters). Privacy: one can select the leaf indexes of the non-pruned FTS at (pseudo)random, but signing a lot will always eventually leak the pruning size. Partial remediation: keep a semi-trusted state S of the previously signed FTS, and when grinding lands on a FTS of S, accept it only with probability (2ᵇ − |S|) / (2ʰ − |S|), so that FTS repeat exactly as often as with a full tree. This essentially gives 2ᵇ⁻¹ signatures with no privacy leak. The state is semi-trusted, because an adversary controlling it can: leak the pruning size, and reduce the lifetime by a factor of 2, but nothing worse. so <@543900561460822016> is it ok we ship PROOF frame and a version of SPHINCS in bogota-03 ? if this is the case we can dismiss daisugi I would go for this, we jsut need to define the specs that we will follow for the PROOF frame. There are currently 3 alternatives/proposals yeah good w me. we will just need to choose what spec to follow for PROOF or sig list I think everyone should spend the next couple days a really look into the options so we can try to decide on ACDT next week thanks, when is next frame breakout room ? No more breakouts for frames, it’s all ACDT and ACDE now we might do the same for PQTS then We need PQ EL breakouts, I like the outcome of the PQ CL ones Awesome. So this gives us https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12714 as the base design to iterate on for bogota-devnet-3 bogota-devnet-2 + PROOF frames* + leanSPHINCS (with no aggregation) = bogota-devnet-3 (of course to be decided on ACDT) + reactivate selfdestruct? excerpts.author: derekchiang
excerpts.content:
not sure if you saw the discussion between <@273808422753796097> and <@1126229231572094976> a few days ago on the 8141 signal chat, but they raised a point that for an account to use leanPCS for authentication, the account contract would need to run PIOP over the PCS claims, but since the PCS claims depend on the sighash, if we run the PIOP in a VERIFY frame (whose calldata is committed to sighash), we have a circular dependency PIOP -> PCS claims -> sighash -> PIOP.  if we run PIOP in a proof frame along with the PCS openings, we lose the benefit of aggregation

so it seems that we'd need either 1) a type of PROOF frame whose calldata is readable from VERIFY frames, or 2) we go back to the siglist design with the ARBITRARY bytes which are readable in VERIFY frames

i personally prefer the siglist approach just because again the proof data is more like dependencies whose ordering doesn't matter.  and to enable L2s to permissionlessly deploy new schemes, maybe we could just replace the siglist scheme ID with verifier address instead?

excerpts.content:
To me its not clear that we can definitively say that we will do PROOF with no aggregation, or PROOF with just builder aggregation or PROOF with mempool aggregation at this point in time.

Though it does seem clear that we need to gather data on the different scenarios where PROOF with no aggregation is the simplest lift from `bogota-devnet-2`. 

Even if we were to go with SPHINCS+, it seems that we will still need to know what are the bandwidth and resource requirements for it, which should hopefully inform us on what is the appropriate size for the signature scheme if the current size is not enough

excerpts.author: niard.eth
excerpts.content:
<@725415098331430932> impact of the parameters on the signature https://ethresear.ch/t/sphincs-minus-efficient-stateless-post-quantum-signature-verification-on-the-evm/25165 

As you can see there is a lot we can do to offload to the signer without losing the lifetime or security level. The one missing piece in that article is pruning which was presented later by conduition https://conduition.io/cryptography/hypertree-pruning/ and basically replaced the "JARDIN" follow up which was a weird smart contract system to have fast signing. 


Solving the privacy problem in pruning courtesy of our Emile : 

Pruning
Use a single, large, XMSS layer. Weak devices only construct a subtree of 2ᵇ leaves, and use pseudorandom nodes for the rest, and signing grinds until its index lands in it (An idea from conduition). Verifier algo is unaffected.

The risk of reusing a seed under different pruning parameters is fixed by deriving a second seed as H(seed ‖ parameters).

Privacy: one can select the leaf indexes of the non-pruned FTS at (pseudo)random, but signing a lot will always eventually leak the pruning size. Partial remediation: keep a semi-trusted state S of the previously signed FTS, and when grinding lands on a FTS of S, accept it only with probability (2ᵇ − |S|) / (2ʰ − |S|), so that FTS repeat exactly as often as with a full tree. This essentially gives 2ᵇ⁻¹ signatures with no privacy leak. The state is semi-trusted, because an adversary controlling it can: leak the pruning size, and reduce the lifetime by a factor of 2, but nothing worse.
